teaser: Web Summit 2026, the plan: usage first, an asset, a page and a link for every person, a summit newsroom, and two agentic workflows.
core_idea: For Web Summit 2026 a five-person team pursues usage before the sale, with five-minute onboarding, public-source intelligence, outreach tailored to one person and content for traffic, all run by one method, an asset, a page and a link, from a Web Summit newsroom of its own, while the team learns the two agentic workflows, starting with the scheduled website workflow because a page is cheap to undo.

figures.caption: Web Summit 2026, usage first, then the sale: intelligence on who to talk to, from public material only; an asset made for one company or one post; a link to it, published on the Web Summit newsroom and sent by email or LinkedIn; usage, five minutes to value in their browser; and what they tell us, pain points from use, not from asking; the next asset is better. The sale comes after the usage, as the RiskMandate customer programme does.

Five people, five tickets, who leads what: the two founders, the story, the products and the sale, approving every message that goes out; the project manager, the board and the rhythm, and the daily follow-up; the Gen AI consultant and technical expert, the demos, the onboarding and the website workflow; the Gen AI founder and explorer coder, the assets built for one company or one post.

The two agentic workflows we run today: the email workflow, agent@riskmandate.ai, where the agent reads, researches, drafts for one person and keeps the records, and the editor reads and sends every draft, the drafts folder a work queue labelled send, review or decide, 178 emails by 18 October; and the website workflow, agents with a role, a policy and a schedule card that wake on their own and release through a gate, 23 agents and 13 schedule cards on the PHP story site.
